subject: Deployment mode follow-up & migration next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@aurora-health.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up & next steps (Aurora Health)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and helpful context on Aurora's migration goals. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Current stack: relying on OpenAI-hosted endpoints for generation + custom prompt orchestration.
- Motivation to migrate: reduce per-token unit cost, get predictable latency at scale, and enable stricter data residency controls for PHI-bound processing.
- Traffic profile (your estimate): ~50 concurrent requests at peak, ~1.5B tokens/month (write-heavy).
- Existing infra: some self-hosted GPU capacity used for local model evals; legacy GPU cluster for overnight batch jobs.

High-level deployment options we discussed (so we're aligned):
1) Hosted API — fastest path for verification and initial pilot. No infra changes; we enforce data controls and SOC2-backed handling on our hosted plane.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pool (single-tenant) for predictable throughput and cost controls; supports autoscaling and private networking hooks. Good for steady production.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — full customer network isolation, optional air-gapped on-prem installs and KMS/HSM integration for regulated workloads.

Attachments: I attached a short PDF that outlines those deployment modes and the typical migration patterns we use (Redwood-Deployment-Modes.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
- Technical deep-dive with Rishi to scope the Dedicated / VPC options and verify integration points (KV cache, prompt stack, auth). Can we target a 60–90 minute session the week of Feb 23?
- If you can share a short infra notes doc (network egress, current auth flows, any compliance constraints) that helps us prepare a migration plan.
- We'll put together a ballpark Dedicated pricing estimate and an optional Hybrid pilot plan (start on Hosted API + move traffic to Dedicated canary).

Let me know availability for the deep-dive and if you'd prefer we draft the SOW or wait until after the tech call.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0142

Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up & next steps (Aurora Health)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. That matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Data residency & PHI: we need logs and raw request/response retention to be under our control for any production path that touches PHI. Is that possible on Dedicated or Private only?
2) Throughput: 50 concurrent requests is a good rough number; some endpoints are heavier (longer contexts). We'd like to target p99 latency under 300ms for short completions (~256 tokens).
3) Migration source: currently using OpenAI + a small self-hosted cluster for model evals. We also have an older GPU cluster that handles batch transforms overnight. We want to avoid a big cutover — prefer a staged migration.

I've attached a short infra notes doc (Aurora-Infra-Notes.docx) with network egress ranges and our SSO metadata. It also lists a brief summary of compliance items we expect in an RFP.

For scheduling, Feb 24 or 25 afternoons PT work for our platform team. We'd appreciate a technical runbook outline before the call if possible.

Thanks,
Alex Tan
Director, Platform Engineering | Aurora Health
alex.tan@aurora-health.com

Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up & next steps (Aurora Health)

Perfect — thanks for the infra doc, Alex.

Quick replies inline:
- Data residency / PHI: Dedicated gives you control over retention windows and a dedicated tenant; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM or kept with customer-managed retention. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control including KMS/HSM. We'll have Neha loop in for a short compliance Q&A.
- Latency: we'll reproduce your p99 target in a tech deep-dive. Depending on model choice/sequence lengths, Dedicated with optimized kernels and our continuous-batching runtime commonly hits that sweet spot.
- Staged migration: agreed — recommended path is: 1) pilot on Hosted API to validate prompts/metrics, 2) move a portion of traffic to Dedicated (canary), 3) if you need network isolation/air-gapped, slide to Private later.

Attached: Redwood-Dedicated-Overview.pdf — includes throughput profiles, typical node sizing, and sample canary rollouts.

Next steps: 
- Rishi and I propose a technical deep-dive on Wednesday, Feb 24 at 1:00 PM PT (60–90m). Confirmed?
- Please list any must-have compliance controls/questions before the call so Neha can prepare.
- We'll prepare a short migration playbook to share before the deep-dive.

If that schedule works, I'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Follow-up: migration approach & technical notes ahead of deep-dive

Alex/Team —

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive. A few technical points and a proposed agenda so we can use the time efficiently: 

Short answers up front:
- Dedicated vs Private: Dedicated is single-tenant capacity we operate for you (network peering + dedicated GPU pools). Private gives you a VPC control plane or fully on-prem install — best for strict compliance/PHI where you need customer-managed keys + no control-plane egress.
- Migration from OpenAI/self-hosted: we support a staged migration. Common approach:
  * Phase 0: acceptance testing on Hosted API (validate prompt behavior and token accounting).
  * Phase 1: traffic split to Dedicated (canary small %). Monitor for drift/regression.
  * Phase 2: bulk cutover after validation; optionally turn on KV cache warmup and prefix caching to reduce cold-starts.
  * Phase 3: if needed, migrate to Private and integrate with your KMS/HSM.

Key integration notes for your team to prepare:
- Tokenization: confirm the tokenizer/model variant you use. We can run a small sample to compare token counts and cost.
- KV cache migration: if you have a cached prompt state, we'll need a small tool to pre-warm caches during the canary.
- Auth & routing: we support SAML/SCIM for enterprise SSO; network peering is via private link or IP allow-listing.
- Observability: we'll give you per-route latency and token usage; logs can stream to your cloud account or to a customer-controlled bucket.

Suggested agenda for the Feb 24 session (60–90m):
1) 10m — intros + objectives
2) 20m — Aurora current infra & constraints (Alex/Vikram)
3) 25m — Redwood architecture deep-dive (Rishi) — Dedicated vs Private
4) 20m — Pilot plan & next steps / Q&A (Marissa + Neha)

I'll attach a short migration-playbook.md that outlines the steps and data we typically collect. It should help you pull together the pre-read items.

Availability: Feb 24, 1:00 PM PT is fine for our team. Sending the invite now.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
